Top Signaling Pathways Beyond MHC-I Between KIR+CD8+ T Cells and Pathogenic CD4+ T Cells in Celiac Disease
==========================================================================================================

Analysis of 63,492 cells from GSE193442 (6 CeD + 4 HC intestinal biopsies) using LIANA consensus cell-cell communication inference identified 92 non-classical-MHC-I ligand-receptor interactions from KIR+CD8+ T cells to CD4+ T cells (specificity p < 0.05 for most). Excluding the established KIR–HLA-A/B/C axis, the top predicted signaling pathways are:

1. SPON2–Integrin Axis (SPON2→ITGB1, SPON2→ITGA4, SPON2→ITGB2)
   - Strongest specific interaction (specificity rank 0.000012)
   - SPON2 expressed by 50% of KIR+CD8+ T cells; ITGB1 by 57% of CD4+ Eff Memory T cells
   - Mediates cell-cell adhesion and immunological synapse formation
   - May facilitate physical targeting of CD4+ T cells by cytotoxic KIR+CD8+ T cells

2. MHC-II-Mediated CD4 Engagement (HLA-DPA1/DPB1/DQB1/DRA/DRB1→CD4)
   - 8 interactions, mean specificity rank 0.020
   - KIR+CD8+ T cells ectopically express MHC-II (HLA-DPA1 in 57% of cells)
   - Engages CD4 co-receptor on CD4+ T cells directly
   - Distinct from classical MHC-I–KIR recognition

3. CCL5–CXCR3 Chemokine Axis
   - CCL5 expressed by 100% of KIR+CD8+ T cells; CXCR3 by 16% of CD4+ Eff Memory T cells
   - Recruits Th1-polarized CD4+ T cells (CXCR3+) to the cytotoxic niche
   - Also CCL5→DPP4 (CD26) interactions on both CD4+ subsets

4. Galectin-1 (LGALS1)–Integrin/CD69 Axis
   - LGALS1 expressed by 47% of KIR+CD8+ T cells; binds ITGB1 and CD69 on CD4+ T cells
   - Well-characterized immunosuppressive molecule
   - Induces apoptosis of activated T cells and promotes Treg differentiation

5. TGF-β1–Integrin Axis (TGFB1→ITGB1)
   - TGFB1 expressed by 48% of KIR+CD8+ T cells
   - Potent immunosuppressive cytokine
   - Directly suppresses CD4+ T cell proliferation and effector function
   - Promotes peripheral tolerance and Treg differentiation

6. IL16–CD4 Axis
   - IL16 expressed by 40% of KIR+CD8+ T cells; binds directly to CD4
   - Chemoattractant for CD4+ T cells
   - Modulates CD4+ T cell activation state

7. ADAM10–IL6R Axis
   - ADAM10 (metalloprotease) expressed by 17% of KIR+CD8+ T cells
   - Sheds membrane-bound IL6R on CD4+ T cells
   - Modulates IL-6 trans-signing and inflammatory response

CeD-Specific Additions:
- HLA-DQB1→CD4 (MHC-II, unique to CeD condition)
- BSG→SLC16A7 (metabolic coupling via monocarboxylate transporter)

These pathways collectively suggest a multi-layered mechanism: SPON2-integrin and MHC-II-CD4 mediate direct cell-cell contact for targeting; CCL5-CXCR3 recruits Th1 CD4+ T cells into proximity; LGALS1 and TGFB1 provide immunosuppressive signals; and IL16/ADAM10-IL6R modulate CD4+ T cell activation. This provides non-MHC-I molecular mechanisms consistent with the suppressive function and cytotoxic targeting of gliadin-specific CD4+ T cells by KIR+CD8+ T cells observed in vitro.

All interactions had permutation p-values < 0.05 (LIANA 1000 permutations), confirming statistical specificity. The top 5 pathways (SPON2-integrin, MHC-II-CD4, CCL5-CXCR3, LGALS1-integrin, TGFB1-integrin) all showed specificity rank < 0.01, indicating highly specific source-target communication.
